source_correspondence: H0–H1 state the normalized second-order matrix family with real scalar principal symbol, original Banach norm, compact nonradial interior segment, full bounded target families and fixed scalar tests. Source order is max(0,q-1), observation order q, target order at most q.

B0 proves ordinary interior smoothing bounds by the actual Banach negative-order estimate. For forcing errors it differentiates the entire input kernel and coefficients in their correct order. It explicitly excludes full boundary residuals from that absorption.

N0 retains fixed nonzero minors through the finite homogeneous canonical completion, smooth parameter flows and inverse charts, exceptional nonzero-momentum integral and conic extension. A finite common parameter neighborhood and nested geometry are selected before every test order.

N1 retains every ordered matrix gauge derivative, full residual recursion and proper-support error. Its Borel radii control compact-parameter seminorms on fixed tubes. The finite-seminorm graph L2 estimate is uniform under the established phase and amplitude bounds.

T0 proves the explicit interval estimate with constants sqrt(length(I)/length(J)) and length(I), positive i primitive sign and averaging of the integration constant. Its distributional version never selects an initial trace.

T1 uses a time-translation-invariant joint-frequency proper kernel, so its differential commutator vanishes exactly. Temporal cutoff derivatives are separated by actual support; all normal-form errors are uniformly ordinary smooth with actual interior input support.

T2 recovers the target with a temporal cutoff supported in the controlled interval. The target times inverse graph has nonpositive order; every inverse and separated-microsupport remainder acts on the original Banach input.

A0–A1 construct fixed scalar source and observation tests for the bounded graph families using complete conic inverses. The source inverse error is applied to P_a u through B0, not discarded or measured in an unfiltered forcing norm.

C0 splits a full boundary target into its ordinary interior part and a complete residual boundary family. The latter is estimated through the exact admissible finite source tree, then all source families are combined by the proved boundary-chart scalar assembly.

C1 proves finite compact interior-ray assembly with one geometric parameter neighborhood, strict overlapping target and observed cones, backward selection of actual observer tests and the same integer q at every step. All sources remain in the prescribed cone.

G0 proves injective actual graph completion by flat transposed kernels and the differential transpose. It makes no graph-density assertion and retains radial, global boundary, wave and full-course obligations.

Three complete solutions check exact interval norms and sharp observation coefficient, the changing-speed Hamilton curves and canonical wave factorization, and a complex nilpotent nonunitary gauge with actual finite bounds.
